title: Bare p8e- prefixed values and the Adobe client-secret subtype they would belong to
summary: A bare value beginning p8e- with a 32-character body, one whose body contains a hyphen, and one in an environment assignment, none under a carrier Adobe names.
rationale: Two rule artifacts of different maintainers treat p8e- plus a 32-character body as an Adobe client secret and name no type (contract claims client-secret-p8e-prefix-consistency and client-secret-p8e-body-length-32, tool-corroborated, consistency only). They differ on whether the body admits a hyphen (claim client-secret-p8e-body-alphabet-hyphen, unresolved), neither cites an Adobe page for the prefix, their independence is unshown (open question p8e-rule-origin-independence), and it is unknown whether every issued secret begins p8e- (p8e-prefix-all-secrets) or which of the S2S, Web App and Enterprise Web App secrets can (p8e-subtype-attribution). Adobe shows only placeholders (s2s-client-secret-docs-placeholders). The named carriers (the client_secret parameter, the Basic envelope) are covered by their own Cases; this case is about the bare value and the subtype, where no outcome is asserted.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Whether a bare value that begins p8e- is an Adobe client secret, of which of the three types, with what body alphabet and for which secrets, is not established by any Adobe page. Settled by an Adobe statement that ties the prefix to a credential type and states the body alphabet and width, an Adobe-published example of a named type, the rule authors' stated basis, or an issuance-gated observation under a maintainer's authority. The vendor-prefix-shaped probe values are intentionally not stored as fixtures (a hosted secret scanner's push protection rejects vendor-shaped literals); a corpus author must assemble such shapes at run time from the shape stated here.

sources.supports: Sample responses for adding a client secret (client_secret shown as a run of X characters) and listing client secrets (uuid and metadata only); the page states no format for the value.
